scales.name: Ionian
scales.source: Piston, Walter & DeVoto, Mark (1987). Harmony, 5th ed. New York: W.W. Norton, ch. 'Modality'.
scales.description: The major scale as a mode; W-W-H-W-W-W-H.

scales.name: Dorian
scales.source: Piston, Walter & DeVoto, Mark (1987). Harmony, 5th ed. New York: W.W. Norton, ch. 'Modality'.
scales.description: Minor with a raised (natural) sixth degree.

scales.name: Phrygian
scales.source: Piston, Walter & DeVoto, Mark (1987). Harmony, 5th ed. New York: W.W. Norton, ch. 'Modality'.
scales.description: Minor with a lowered second degree.

scales.name: Lydian
scales.source: Piston, Walter & DeVoto, Mark (1987). Harmony, 5th ed. New York: W.W. Norton, ch. 'Modality'.
scales.description: Major with a raised fourth degree.

scales.name: Mixolydian
scales.source: Piston, Walter & DeVoto, Mark (1987). Harmony, 5th ed. New York: W.W. Norton, ch. 'Modality'.
scales.description: Major with a lowered seventh degree.

scales.name: Aeolian
scales.source: Piston, Walter & DeVoto, Mark (1987). Harmony, 5th ed. New York: W.W. Norton, ch. 'Modality'.
scales.description: The natural minor scale as a mode.

scales.name: Locrian
scales.source: Piston, Walter & DeVoto, Mark (1987). Harmony, 5th ed. New York: W.W. Norton, ch. 'Modality'.
scales.description: Minor with lowered second and fifth degrees; the only mode with a diminished tonic triad.

scales.name: Harmonic Minor
scales.source: Piston, Walter & DeVoto, Mark (1987). Harmony, 5th ed. New York: W.W. Norton, ch. 'The Minor Mode'.
scales.description: Natural minor with a raised leading tone, producing the characteristic augmented second between the sixth and seventh degrees.

scales.name: Melodic Minor (ascending)
scales.source: Piston, Walter & DeVoto, Mark (1987). Harmony, 5th ed. New York: W.W. Norton, ch. 'The Minor Mode'.
scales.description: Ascending form only, per the plan: natural minor with raised sixth and seventh degrees. Restyling is pitch remapping, not a contour-aware ascending/descending distinction, so only the ascending collection is authored.

scales.name: Double Harmonic (Byzantine)
scales.source: Slonimsky, Nicolas (1947). Thesaurus of Scales and Melodic Patterns. New York: Coleman-Ross, 'Heptatonic Scales with Two Augmented Seconds'.
scales.description: Also called the Arabic/Byzantine scale and, in Western terms, Hijaz Kar: two augmented-second gaps, between degrees 2-3 and 6-7.

scales.name: Hungarian Minor
scales.source: Slonimsky, Nicolas (1947). Thesaurus of Scales and Melodic Patterns. New York: Coleman-Ross, 'Heptatonic Scales with Two Augmented Seconds'.
scales.description: Harmonic minor with a raised fourth degree; also called the Gypsy minor scale.

scales.name: Ukrainian Dorian
scales.source: Slonimsky, Nicolas (1947). Thesaurus of Scales and Melodic Patterns. New York: Coleman-Ross, 'Heptatonic Scales with One Augmented Second'.
scales.description: Dorian with a raised fourth degree; also called the Romanian minor / altered Dorian scale.
